_meta.label: AI-generated data file: built by code written with an AI assistant (Claude Code). No language model ran to build it. Counts, recorded ranges and grouped cross-validation errors are computed by code from NASA PSI tables (data/pipeline/tests.csv); the verdicts are fixed rules applied by code. Team output, not a NASA conclusion. No fitted model or model output is in this file.

title: Can these NASA tables support an outcome model?
fixed_line: None is a cabin-material flammability model.
labels_and_limits: The team's statistical diagnostics on NASA PSI tables. They describe the experiments in these tables only. FLEX extinction is a droplet-flame outcome, not material flammability. "Indicative" means a simple model beat the base rate under 5-fold grouped cross-validation, nothing more. No fitted model, coefficient or model output is shipped, and none is offered for any condition, inside or outside the recorded ranges.
counts_note: Counts are recorded tests in NASA's open PSI experimental tables, the team's computation. 'Not recorded' is never zero and never 101 kPa.
flag_rule: Cells that carry a flag in the flags column of data/pipeline/tests.csv are left out. A test is not counted in a row when its label cell, its test id, or any condition cell the row needs (listed in 'required_cells') is flagged or empty; each row gives these exclusions in 'excluded'. A recorded range uses only unflagged, non-empty cells, and 'range_values_n' gives how many.
basis_rule: Rows are split by o2_basis and never pooled: 'ambient' is the oxygen of the surrounding atmosphere, 'oxidizer_stream' is the oxygen of the gas issuing from the burner (CFI-G inverse flames). Burner-stream oxygen is not a habitat atmosphere and is never compared with ambient oxygen.
verdict_rule: Fixed in code before any number was computed. 'too few' if a label has fewer than 100 tests, fewer than 20 groups, or a class with fewer than 20 tests; then no cross-validation is run. Otherwise 5-fold grouped cross-validation (scikit-learn GroupKFold, shuffled groups, seed 20261114): the simple model 'beats the base rate on held-out conditions (indicative)' when its mean fold error is lower than the baseline's by more than the larger of the two fold standard deviations; otherwise it is 'no better than the base rate'. Errors: Brier score for a class label (lower is better), mean absolute error for a numeric label (lower is better).

rows.label: FLEX droplet extinction-to-initial diameter ratio (tests that ended in extinction, ratio above 0)
rows.grouping_rule: FLEX condition group: fuel, oxygen rounded to 1%, pressure in atmospheres (kPa / 101.325) rounded to 0.1, and diluent (nitrogen only, carbon dioxide added, helium added). Repeat tests at one condition are never split across training and held-out folds.

model.name: linear regression (scikit-learn, standardised numbers, one-hot fuel)

rows.verdict: simple model beats the base rate on held-out conditions (indicative)
rows.reason: 5-fold grouped cross-validation over 65 groups: mean absolute error of the simple model 0.126 (fold standard deviation 0.0276) against 0.1875 (fold standard deviation 0.013) for the baseline; the rule asks for a lower error by more than 0.0276. Held-out groups are conditions the model did not see in training, inside the recorded ranges of this table only.

rows.reason: The BASS-II table writes a flow event only for the 25 tests in which one was noted; the other tests have an empty cell, which does not say that no event happened. So there is no recorded 'no' class to learn from.

No table has a partial-gravity test: every test row in the team's tests.csv is recorded at microgravity (gravity level set per table by the team from the PSI record). Microgravity and 1 g results are not bounds for lunar or Martian gravity.
